{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Derrick Corson Niederman''' is an [[author]], [[mathematician]], [[game designer]], and national squash champion.  His most recent game, [[36 cube|36 Cube]],<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.thinkfun.com/36cube/index.html |title=36Cube Homepage |access-date=2008-12-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081219205115/http://www.thinkfun.com/36Cube/index.html |archive-date=2008-12-19 |url-status=dead }}</ref> has been described by [[Reuters]] as "a wolf in sheep's clothing"<ref name="Reuters">{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130201222152/http://www.reuters.com/article/pressRelease/idUS144246+19-Nov-2008+PRN20081119|title=Reuters}}</ref> because its simple design belies the sophisticated mathematical intuition required for the solution. He received a B.A. in mathematics from [[Yale]] and a Ph.D. in mathematics from [[MIT]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.randomhouse.ca/catalog/display.pperl?isbn=9780307419569 |title=RandomHouse.ca {{!}} Books {{!}} What the Numbers Say by Derrick Niederman and David Boyum |website=www.randomhouse.ca |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120306030028/http://www.randomhouse.ca/catalog/display.pperl?isbn=9780307419569 |archive-date=2012-03-06}} </ref> Dr. Niederman is a math professor at the [[College of Charleston]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://magazine.cofc.edu/2012/06/12/derrick_niederman/|title=Put Together: The Enigmatic World of Derrick Niederman|date=12 June 2012}}</ref> In 2025, Niederman founded Wordsmith Games. The flagship game is called Tosswords. <ref>https://wordsmithgames.com/about-us/</ref>

==Published games==
[[File:36Cube.JPG|thumb|36 Cube]]
'''''The New York Times Magazine'' Sunday Crosswords'''

Niederman has created a number of crossword puzzles and cryptic puzzles for ''[[The New York Times Magazine]]'' since the early 1980s. His October 5, 1997 crossword puzzle "Baseball by the Numbers" is often included in crossword puzzle anthologies.<ref>{{Cite book | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=09DtD5EP41AC&q=derrick+niederman+baseball+by+the+numbers&pg=PT52 | title=The New York Times Supersized Book of Sunday Crosswords: 500 Puzzles| isbn=9780312361228| last1=Shortz| first1=Will| last2=Maleska| first2=Eugene T.| date=2006-09-19}}</ref>

'''Puzzle and Game Books'''

Dr. Niederman has also published other game and puzzle books.

* ''The Puzzler's Dilemma'' (2012)
* ''Math Puzzles for the Clever Mind'' (2006)
* ''Hard to Solve Math Puzzles'' (2006)
* ''Classic Brain Twisters'' (2005)
* ''Mind-Stretching Math Puzzles'' (2005)
* ''Sit & Solve Brainteasers'' (2003)
* ''Hard-to-Solve Math Puzzles'' (2001)
* ''Giant Book of Whodunit Puzzles and Giant Book of Puzzles for Young Einsteins'' (2001)
* ''Pocket Puzzlers: Whodunits'' (2000)
* ''The Little Giant Book of Math Puzzles'' (2000)

'''36 Cube'''
                                                                                                      
The [[36 cube|36 Cube]] is a puzzle that requires the arrangement of "towers" in a 6x6 square block so that each color appears only once in each row and column, all the same height.  The completed puzzle will then be a cube.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.thinkfun.com/36cube/instructions.html |title=Instructions |access-date=2008-12-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081211113604/http://www.thinkfun.com/36Cube/instructions.html |archive-date=2008-12-11 |url-status=dead }}</ref>  [[Jerry Slocum]], a puzzle historian and one of the world's top puzzle collectors, finds [[36 cube|36 Cube]] one of the most engaging puzzles in his extensive collection. "My first impression was that it was quite a beautiful puzzle. Its three-dimensional character and colors are very striking. Out of the 30,000 puzzles I own, it's quite distinctive and unique."<ref name="Reuters"/> Dr. Niederman came up with the idea while writing a book on whole numbers, after unearthing a mathematical supposition from the 18th century. "It struck me as the basis for a potentially great 3-D puzzle, and what eventually became [[36 cube|36 Cube]]."<ref name="Reuters"/>

'''Wordsmith Games'''

Niederman founded Wordsmith Games in early 2025; its flagship game, called Tosswords, began production in the fall of that year.<ref>https://wordsmithgames.com/</ref>
